Five comments

Wearied Lad

This interesting slide appears in The Petrie Collection of Irish Music, part II, ed. Charles Villiers Stanford (1905), p. 137, no. 541 as “The wearied lad. Set by Lord Rosmore from P. Coneely 1843”. Patrick Coneely was a famous Galway piper.
The transcription is due to AK/Fiddler’s Companion that says “There may be some relation to the “Gold Ring” family of tunes”. This tune is also know as “Limerick Tinker”, “Bouchalaun Buie”, “Yellow Ragweed” .

↳ Posted by Moxhe on November 9th, 2015.

The Gold Ring

Although this is clearly derived from the usual 6-part version in G ( https://thesession.org/tunes/37 ), it really is different enough to warrant its own inclusion here. Transcribed from Edel Fox, Neill Byrne and Macdara Ó Faoláin:
https://youtu.be/kM9ky8y4C9w?si=W8bJCNTfILD2hKyz&t=1273

↳ Posted by coppers and brass on August 19th, 2023.

The Gold Ring, X:4

Paddy O’Brien (Offaly) has this in his Tune Collection (volume 3, jig #50)
as The Wearied Lad. A slide version from the Petrie collection is at https://thesession.org/tunes/14933
where it says it’s from the piping of Paddy Conneely 1843. Paddy O’Brien says that’s where it came from
and that he remembers learning it from “the late great fiddler Dan Cleary of Ballinamere, Co. Offaly”.

I immediately noticed the similarity to The Gold Ring and so posted Paddy’s version here.
Paddy’s setting is A B C B whereas Edel puts in a part of the more common Gold Ring for the
fourth part.

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on December 28th, 2025.
